name: veterinary_clinic_system_009_rabies_certificate_doc_check
instruction: Run the rabies-certificate document audit for the practice as of the episode date. In this jurisdiction, rabies certificates are required for dogs and cats only. (1) For every files row with doc_type='rabies-certificate', set doc_status to 'current' if that patient is a canine or feline whose latest rabies vaccination due_date is on or after the episode date; otherwise set it to 'stale'. Do not change any other field on those rows and do not touch non-rabies file rows. (2) For every canine or feline patient that has a current (not overdue) rabies vaccination and still has no rabies-certificate file row after step 1, push a placeholder certificate: bucket='vet-documents', path='{patient_id}/rabies-certificate/pending-{batch_code}.pdf', patient_id, doc_type='rabies-certificate', filename='pending-{batch_code}.pdf', content_type='application/pdf', size_bytes=0, uploaded_by='system', uploaded_at the episode timestamp, doc_status='current'. (3) For each dog or cat that receives a placeholder, send one outbound email communication to the owner: channel='email', direction='outbound', subject='Rabies certificate missing — {batch_code}', body='{PatientName} (patient {patient_id}) is missing a current rabies certificate as of {episode date YYYY-MM-DD}.', logged_by='system', occurred_at the episode timestamp, owner_id and patient_id set. (4) Push exactly one ops_reports row with report='rabies_certificate_audit' and the live batch_code, containing the computed aggregates and a by_location breakdown: total_rabies_dogs_cats, current_rabies, stale_rabies, current_with_certificate, current_missing_certificate, stale_with_certificate, placeholders_created, communications_sent, and by_location (per location: total, current, stale, with_cert, missing, stale_cert). If an ops_reports row for this report and batch_code already exists, overwrite it. The flow is idempotent.

success_criteria.summary: Episode date from ops_meta. Existing rabies-certificate file rows get doc_status 'current' or 'stale' based on the patient's latest rabies due_date vs episode, with all non-doc_status fields unchanged. One placeholder file is pushed for every current-rabies canine/feline that has no certificate, with path/filename embedding the live batch_code and exact remaining fields. One outbound email is pushed per placeholder, keyed by patient_id because owner names/pet names can collide. Exactly one ops_reports row (report='rabies_certificate_audit', batch_code) holds the counts and by_location breakdown, with all aggregates verified via dual raw-row and SQL paths. All collections outside the blast radius are byte-identical to the seed snapshot.

checks.expect: Every existing rabies-certificate row has correct doc_status; all non-certificate rows unchanged; exactly one placeholder per current-rabies canine/feline without a certificate
Exactly one new outbound email per placeholder recipient, matched by patient_id and subject containing the batch_code
Exactly one row with report='rabies_certificate_audit' and the batch_code, all aggregate and per-location numbers correct
Every aggregate count in ops_reports agrees between a raw-row Python filter over live data and an independent SQL GROUP BY/COUNT query

hazards: Non-required species with current rabies: the seed snapshot has 127 dogs and cats with a rabies record (103 current, 24 stale as of 2026-09-30), plus 5 avians, 4 equines, and 7 exotics with current rabies. Only canines and felines are in scope; species outside those two must not receive placeholder files or communications.

Existing non-rabies files: the seed files collection contains 7 non-rabies rows (radiograph, clinical photo, boarding-consent, anesthesia-consent, referral-letter). An over-broad 'add doc_status to every file' or 'touch every files row' mutation changes these and fails the canary check.

Multi-pet owner name collision: the 50-name pet pool and 103 current-rabies dogs/cats mean two different pets of the same owner can share the same name. The verifier matches placeholder and communication rows by patient_id, not by pet name or owner name.

Date boundary around the episode: three current-rabies dogs/cats have due_dates in the jitter-sensitive band [2026-09-27, 2026-10-03] (patient 121/2026-09-30, 208/2026-09-30, 288/2026-10-01). The 'current' test must use '>=' vs episode date; at jitter +3 (ep 2026-10-03) one fewer current patient qualifies than at the base date.

Idempotency on re-run: a second run must see the placeholders and communications it already created and skip them, update the same existing cert doc_status, overwrite (not duplicate) the ops_reports row, and leave the final state byte-identical to the first run.
